families.notes: Not the front structure: the crowd's first buy is not predictable in time (+68..+204), the pull is not a fixed margin after it, and several sniper bots already trade these pools. The edge is a ride on a crowd that buys with minOut 0 in bursts. The mean is driven by bursts (p90 +41%), so variance is high and the sample is 203 pools in 2 days, with the 4.6% stake-loss rate measured where snipers are present. Low confidence; the score is the with-sniper ride number. Scripts: deep_crowd.py, slices_crowd.py, fine_grid.py, cond_crowd.py.

families.notes: A different operator type from the vbot: a scripted crowd that pumps steadily with minOut 0 and a slow, mostly absent pull (70% not pulled within 3,000 blocks). It is not the front/quick-pull structure, so the literal rules fail, but the ride is clean: 97.9% win, about 1% of stakes lost, stable across time. The open question is the same one v2.433 had before going live: no real-size outsider has ever bought ahead of this crowd, so whether the operator pulls on one is unknown. The score is the add +1 to add +180 ride. Longer holds price higher (+65% mean at 1,000 blocks) but lose 18% of stakes. Scripts: deep_crowd.py, slices_crowd.py, fine_grid.py, cond_crowd.py, trap_extra.py, fetch_adds.py (192 add txs fetched).
